# What 0212 converted, and the guard that keeps the relocated corpus honest.
#
# Before 0212 the corpus lived under the work skill's bash test-fixtures tree
# and the parity tests shelled out to the scripts. 0212 relocated every fixture
# into per-crate tests/fixtures/ trees and rewrote the tests to read them
# directly. This file now guards the relocated layout.
#
# Three kinds of row.
#
# `test` rows name the pure-Rust parity tests that read a committed corpus,
# with the number of `#[test]` functions each carries and the corpus it reads.
#
# `case` rows record the SET of case directories per corpus. The per-directory
# counts are DERIVED from these names by bash_parity_baseline.rs and printed in
# its failure message — storing the numbers too is how the numeric copy goes
# stale. The guard compares SETS, not a total: a bare count is both too strict
# (an unrelated fixture reds the build) and too loose (a delete plus an add nets
# the same total and passes while the drift goes through). Each corpus resolves
# to its per-crate home via corpus_home() in the reader.
#
# `hash` rows record the sha256 of every committed golden/expected file,
# repo-relative. This is the byte-identity guard: the converted parity tests
# check the Rust recipe against these goldens, and without a hash manifest a
# future regeneration of code-and-golden together would pass tautologically.
# The goldens ARE the frozen bash oracle and must never be regenerated from
# Rust output; a changed byte reds every_committed_golden_matches_its_hash.
#
# The corpus has two provenances that both predate 0212:
# work-item-project-remote/ came from 0170, work-item-sync-baseline/ from 0194.

test  cli/work/tests/normalise_parity.rs                  4   work-item-normalise

test  cli/work-adapters/tests/sync_working_copy_status.rs 7   (no committed fixture)
test  cli/work-cli/tests/cli_diff_parity.rs               3   work-item-section-diff
test  cli/remote-projection/tests/parity.rs               4   work-item-project-remote
